questions.question: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. He flatters the boss to his face but criticises him in his absence .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

He flatters the boss to his face but criticises him in his absence.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 'behind his back'.

Key Points

  • The phrase "behind his back" means to do something without someone's knowledge, typically in a deceitful or sneaky manner. (पीठ पीछे)
    • Example: She found out that they had been talking about her behind her back.
  • "behind his back" is an idiom that implies actions or words that are kept secret from the person concerned and are usually negative or critical. (पीठ पीछे)
    • Example: He was upset when he learned that his friends were making fun of him behind his back.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 'behind his back'.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • At random (बिना किसी क्रम के): Without a specific pattern, order, or objective.
    • Example: The winner was chosen at random from a list of participants.
  • Behind the scenes (पर्दे के पीछे): In secret, especially in a way that is not public knowledge.
    • Example: Many negotiations took place behind the scenes before the deal was finalized.
  • At home (घर पर): In one's own residence.
    • Example: She prefers to work at home rather than in an office.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate idiomatic expression that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Today's managers' meeting has given me a lot to think about as I decide whether or not to stay with this company.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate idiomatic expression that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Today's managers' meeting has given me a lot to think about as I decide whether or not to stay with this company.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. food for thought.

Key Points

  • The phrase "roll with the punches" means to adapt to difficult circumstances. (मुसीबतों का सामना करना)
    • Example: In business, you have to learn to roll with the punches and keep moving forward.
  • "bird's eye view" refers to a general view from above, or an overall perspective of something. (ऊपर से देखने पर पूरी तस्वीर)
    • Example: The strategic plan gave us a bird's eye view of the company's future direction.
  • "belle of the ball" refers to the most attractive woman at a gathering. (सभी का ध्यान आकर्षित करने वाली महिला)
    • Example: She was the belle of the ball at last night's gala event.
  • "food for thought" means something that warrants serious consideration. (गहन विचार के योग्य)
    • Example: The presentation provided a lot of food for thought regarding our marketing strategy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: food for thought.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Roll with the punches (मुसीबतों का सामना करना): To adapt to difficult circumstances.
    • Example: In business, you have to learn to roll with the punches and keep moving forward.
  • Bird's eye view (ऊपर से देखने पर पूरी तस्वीर): A general view from above, or an overall perspective of something.
    • Example: The strategic plan gave us a bird's eye view of the company's future direction.
  • Belle of the ball (सभी का ध्यान आकर्षित करने वाली महिला): The most attractive woman at a gathering.
    • Example: She was the belle of the ball at last night's gala event.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the underlined idiom/phrase in the given sentence. He threw cold water over the project that the secretary had prepared.
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the meaning of the underlined idiom/phrase in the given sentence.

He threw cold water over the project that the secretary had prepared.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'discouraged​'

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the idiom 'throw cold water on something' means 'to discourage or deter something.'
    • Example:
      • Ravi is always throwing cold water on my suggestions.
      • He throws cold water on our pleasures every time we come out to enjoy.
  • Hence, the correct answer is Discouraged.

Additional Information

  • Let's explore the other options:
  • Encouraged: to give hope, support, or confidence to somebody​ (किसी को) प्रोत्‍साहित करना; (किसी की) हिम्‍मत बढ़ाना
  • Examples:
    • She shouldn't have encouraged Alex to come down here.
    • He nodded, apparently encouraged by her smile.
    • He'd probably just say I encouraged him.

questions.question: Directions: Given below are some idioms/phrases followed by four alternative meanings to each. Select the response (a), (b), (c) or (d), which is the most appropriate meaning and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly. Have the last laugh
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Given below are some idioms/phrases followed by four alternative meanings to each. Select the response (a), (b), (c) or (d), which is the most appropriate meaning and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly. 

Have the last laugh

options.text: to be the worst example of something
options.html: to be the worst example of something

options.text: to succeed when others thought that you would not
options.html: to succeed when others thought that you would not

options.text: to solve all the problems of life
options.html: to solve all the problems of life

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2.

Key Points

  • The idiom "have the last laugh" means:
    • To succeed when others thought that you would not. (अंत में सफल होना जब दूसरे सोचते थे कि आप सफल नहीं होंगे)
  • Example: Despite all the criticism, she had the last laugh by winning the championship.
    • हिंदी में: सभी आलोचनाओं के बावजूद, उसने चैंपियनशिप जीतकर अंत में सफल हुई।

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • To be the worst example of something (किसी चीज़ का सबसे खराब उदाहरण होना):
    • Example: The company is the worst example of how to manage resources.
    • हिंदी में: कंपनी संसाधनों को प्रबंधित करने का सबसे खराब उदाहरण है।
  • To solve all the problems of life (जीवन की सभी समस्याओं को हल करना):
    • Example: Winning the lottery won't solve all the problems of life.
    • हिंदी में: लॉटरी जीतने से जीवन की सभी समस्याएं हल नहीं होंगी।
  • To laugh at someone secretly (किसी पर गुप्त रूप से हंसना):
    • Example: They laughed at his mistakes secretly.
    • हिंदी में: उन्होंने उसकी गलतियों पर गुप्त रूप से हंसा।

questions.question: Select the appropriate meaning of the given Idiom. In hot water
questions.questionHtml:
Select the appropriate meaning of the given Idiom.

In hot water
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Trouble with someone' (Option 4).

 Key Points

  • The idiom "In hot water" has nothing to do with actual water. It is an English idiom that means "in trouble" or "facing difficulties or criticism".
  • The phrase likely comes from the age-old practice of heating water for bathing, where being "in hot water" could be uncomfortable or dangerous.
  • The other choices, "Medically useful water", "Water in turbulence", "Water getting hot suddenly" do not express the actual idiomatic meaning of "in hot water".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 Additional Information

Idioms can be very interesting and sometimes fun phrases that add colour to language. However, because their meanings are usually metaphorical and don't decode literally, they can pose challenges to non-native speakers.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. Despite their differences, the counties found common ground and buried the hatchet .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

Despite their differences, the counties found common ground and buried the hatchet.

options.text: To seek revenge in the future
options.html: To seek revenge in the future

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3.

Key Points

  • The idiom "to bury the hatchet" means to settle a dispute or conflict and become reconciled. (मतभेदों को समाप्त करना और मेल-मिलाप करना)
    • Example: After years of rivalry, the two companies decided to bury the hatchet and collaborate on a new project.
  • "To continue a conflict" means to keep on fighting or disagreeing. (संघर्ष जारी रखना)
    • Example: The two neighbors continued their conflict over the property line for years.
  • "To disagree publicly" means to show disagreement openly. (सार्वजनिक रूप से असहमति व्यक्त करना)
    • Example: The politicians disagreed publicly on the new policy.
  • "To seek revenge in the future" means to plan to get back at someone later. (भविष्य में बदला लेने की योजना बनाना)
    • Example: He pretended to forgive his rival but planned to seek revenge in the future.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 1: To continue a conflict (संघर्ष जारी रखना): To keep on fighting or disagreeing.
    • Example: The two neighbors continued their conflict over the property line for years.
  • Option 2: To disagree publicly (सार्वजनिक रूप से असहमति व्यक्त करना): To show disagreement openly.
    • Example: The politicians disagreed publicly on the new policy.
  • Option 4: To seek revenge in the future (भविष्य में बदला लेने की योजना बनाना): To plan to get back at someone later.
    • Example: He pretended to forgive his rival but planned to seek revenge in the future.

questions.question: Identify the correct meaning of the idiom(s) given below. At the drop of a hat
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the correct meaning of the idiom(s) given below.

At the drop of a hat
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Without any hesitation; immediately.".

Key Points

  • The idiom 'At the drop of a hat' is used to describe a situation where something is done instantly, without any delay, or without a significant reason.
  • It means doing something immediately, without hesitation.
  • For example, if we say, "He would leave work at the drop of a hat to help his family," it means he would leave work immediately without hesitation to assist his family if needed.
  • Hence, the correct answer will be Option 2.

questions.question: Directions : Choose appropriate meaning of the idiom from the choices given. To move heaven and earth

To move heaven and earth
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: To try everything possible.

Key Points

  • Let's understand the meaning of the given idiom

      • ​Example: She will move heaven and earth to pass the exam.
  • ​​Thus, from the options given, To try everything possible is correct.

​The correct answer is: option 2, To try everything possible.
